CDbw.scientific_definition_source: Halkidi & Vazirgiannis (2008), 'A density-based cluster validity approach using multi-representatives', Pattern Recognition Letters 29, 773-786
CDbw.code_relationship: PAPER-FAITHFUL CORRECTION LAYER over the MIT package (geometry reused with attribution; three aggregations replaced)
CDbw.parameter_policy: package defaults, pinned before any external outcome was seen; never tuned

algebraic_identities_against_the_package.note: both ratios are predicted in advance by the two defects and observed exactly

validation.independent_cross_check: CRAN fpc::cdbw is permutation-invariant (spread 0.0 over cluster-order permutations); it uses a different representative construction so it is not a numeric oracle for our value

label_order_finding.finding: the package is NOT invariant to the integer ordering of cluster labels, although the published index is defined over an unordered set of clusters
label_order_finding.root_cause: prep() returns the highest-indexed cluster standard deviation instead of the average over clusters, contradicting its own docstring; separation() additionally minimises over lower-indexed clusters only
label_order_finding.resolution: the aggregations were corrected, so CDbw is now permutation-invariant by construction and no ordering convention is used
label_order_finding.reporting_requirement: CDbw values produced by the raw package without a stated cluster ordering are not comparable to ours, nor to each other

CVNN.scientific_definition_source: Liu, Li, Xiong, Gao, Wu (2013), 'Understanding and enhancement of internal clustering validation measures', IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics 43(3), 982-994
CVNN.documented_variant: CVNN as defined in Liu et al. (2013) with the correction described in Halkidi et al. (2015), per the fpc documentation
CVNN.code_relationship: EXTERNAL VALIDATION ORACLE ONLY -- no fpc source is copied or ported, to avoid incorporating GPL obligations
CVNN.parameter_policy: fpc documented default k=5, frozen before any external outcome
CVNN.why_the_earlier_search_missed_it: the Stage-4A/first-4B search queried PyPI and GitHub only. CVNN's maintained reference lives on CRAN, an R repository that neither query covers, and the one Python package inspected (validclust) provides dunn/cop/silhouette/DB/CH but NOT cvnn. The conclusion 'no reference exists' was therefore drawn from an incomplete search space, not from evidence of absence.
CVNN.bug_found_and_fixed_before_any_scientifi: K=1 candidate partitions were being excluded before the component normalisers were computed. fpc includes them in max(sep)/max(comp), so excluding them shifted every other candidate's value. Fixed; the oracle is what surfaced it.

CVDD.scientific_definition_source: Hu & Zhong (2019), 'An Internal Validity Index Based on Density-Involved Distance', IEEE Access 7, 40038-40051, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2019.2906949
CVDD.reference_bundled_data: Datasets_all30/ -- 30 labelled datasets with ground truth, usable as author-provided validation examples
CVDD.code_relationship: PORT UNDER LICENCE with attribution (MIT permits this)
CVDD.parameter_policy: authors state no parameter tuning is required
CVDD.why_the_earlier_search_missed_it: the GitHub query used was 'CVDD+cluster+validity', which returned 0 hits; the repository is named simply 'CVDD' and its description does not contain that phrase. The search was too narrow, and absence of hits was wrongly treated as absence of a reference.

frozen_applicability_rule.rule: if X contains two or more EXACTLY identical rows, CVDD is INVALID with reason CVDD_DUPLICATE_POINT_MST_AMBIGUITY
frozen_applicability_rule.duplicate_definition: exact row equality; deliberately no epsilon, which would add an arbitrary metric parameter
frozen_applicability_rule.rationale: the density-involved distance rests on a minimax path distance from a minimum spanning tree; exact duplicates create zero-weight edges, the MST is then non-unique, and the published procedure defines no implementation-independent tie-break, so no canonical CVDD value exists for such an input
frozen_applicability_rule.evidence: duplicates_2 fixture: 80 points, 60 unique, 40 zero off-diagonal distances; Prim and Kruskal select different equally-minimal trees
frozen_applicability_rule.scope: invalidates CVDD ONLY -- never the dataset, view, another CVI, a method run, or fixed32 candidate generation

DCSI.scientific_definition_source: Gauss, Scheipl & Herrmann, 'DCSI - An improved measure of cluster separability based on separation and connectedness'
DCSI.license_finding: NO explicit licence declared in the repository
DCSI.code_relationship: INDEPENDENT REIMPLEMENTATION FROM THE PAPER ONLY. No source line copied, vendored or adapted. The repository is used solely as an external numerical oracle in a temporary checkout that is never committed, and no author data is committed either.
DCSI.diagnostic_variant: dcsi_author_compat (AUTHOR_COMPAT) -- not a comparator, not a fifth CVI
DCSI.parameter_policy: no tuning on the external corpus

validation.level: component-wise (core points, connectedness, separation, pairwise index, aggregate)

paper_vs_reference_discrepancy.summary: the repository holds two DCSI routines; the two-class routine matches Definition 3.2 and produced the published values we recomputed, while the multiclass real-world routine doubles every separation entry via its symmetrisation step
paper_vs_reference_discrepancy.publication_value_reproduction: PAPER (max abs diff 1.11e-16 on two end-to-end recomputable cases)
paper_vs_reference_discrepancy.ranking_equivalence: holds for K=2 only; refuted for K>=3 analytically and empirically

needed_for: DCSI via the author's R code
